summary: The Playwright test file is syntactically correct and uses Playwright APIs properly, but has some issues related to selector quality, assertion strength, and maintainability. Selectors like /product/i and /related product/i in getByRole may be too generic or weak, potentially leading to flaky tests. Some assertions rely on text matching which could be brittle. Navigation assertions rely on regex matching without verifying the actual product context. The test titles correctly preserve testCaseIds. No asynchronous assertion lacks await. No locator misuse detected.

issues.description: Selectors using regex like /product/i in getByRole('link', { name: /product/i }) might be too generic, risking flaky tests if multiple matches occur.
issues.recommendation: Use more specific text or attributes for getByRole selectors to precisely identify the intended elements.

issues.description: Navigation assertions use generic URL regex like /detail/ or /related-detail/ which may not sufficiently verify navigation to the correct product detail page.
issues.recommendation: Enhance navigation assertions with more precise URL patterns or verify page content reflects the targeted product.

issues.description: Assertions on getByText for static strings like /category badge/i or /brand badge/i assume these texts are present exactly, which may not be robust.
issues.recommendation: Consider using more stable selectors or additional attributes such as test ids for badges.

recommendations: Refine selectors to be more specific and stable.
Improve assertion strategies for verifying correct page navigation and product details.
Consider adding helper functions or test data abstraction for maintainability.
